primary_new_sources.title: Tight DRAM Supply Gives Suppliers Greater Pricing Power in HBM, with HBM Contract Prices Expected to Surge Multiples Higher in 2027, Says TrendForce
supported: TrendForce says its per-wafer revenue analysis uses die size, yield rates and per-Gb pricing; this is a wafer-revenue comparison, not a direct 3:1 bit conversion.

Estimated HBM wafer input among top three suppliers is approximately 18%/22%/30% of total DRAM wafer input at end-2025/2026/2027; HBM bit supply approximately 8%/9%/13% of total DRAM bit supply for the same years.
TrendForce explicitly expects the conventional-DRAM crowding-out effect to intensify in 2027 as HBM generations use larger die and demand rises.

numerical_basis.denominator: top-three suppliers' HBM share of total DRAM wafer input/bit supply; industry-level, not Nanya
numerical_basis.unit_warning: wafer-input percentages and bit-output percentages have different denominators; do not subtract or convert without die/yield/node assumptions

primary_new_sources.counterevidence_or_limit: No supplier-by-supplier allocation, Nanya share, conventional DRAM wafer reduction, node, DDR product split, or customer order amount. HBM wafer-input share is not equivalent to HBM bit share because die size/yield differ.

primary_new_sources.title: [News] Samsung Sees HBM Taking Nearly 30% of Industry DRAM Capacity in 2027, Up From 20% Currently
supported: TrendForce reports Reuters' account of Samsung EVP Kim Taewoo: HBM could be nearly 30% of total DRAM industry wafer capacity in 2027 versus about 20% currently; HBM and conventional DRAM compete for the same wafer capacity.
The same article cites ijiwei that HBM consumes roughly three times the wafer area of conventional DRAM and that one HBM die's area is roughly equivalent to 3GB DDR5 area.

numerical_basis.area_claim: approximately 3x conventional DRAM wafer area; secondary cited estimate, not an Nanya measurement
numerical_basis.unit_warning: '3x wafer area' and '3GB DDR5 equivalent die area' are not a same-bits, same-yield wafer conversion; source does not provide Nanya node or product mix

primary_new_sources.counterevidence_or_limit: Curated secondary article, not a direct Samsung filing; Samsung/industry figures cannot be assigned to Nanya. It also says 8-Hi uses fewer DRAM dies and supports the same HBM bit output across more GPUs, so stack height changes die/bit demand without proving wafer reduction for 2408.

primary_new_sources.title: [News] Micron Flags HBM4E as Start of Custom HBM Era; HBM Market Could Tilt Toward Dual-or-Single Suppliers
supported: TrendForce relays Micron EVP Sumit Sadana's 3:1 HBM3E-to-DDR trade-off: 100 bits of HBM3E effectively sacrifices around 300 bits of DDR supply; HBM4/HBM4E expected to worsen toward nearly 4:1.
Micron says it is using 1-beta DRAM for HBM4 and expects 1-gamma for HBM4E, illustrating node/product specificity.

numerical_basis.same_bits_tradeoff: 100 HBM3E bits : approximately 300 DDR bits (3:1 sacrificed DDR bits)
numerical_basis.future_ratio: near 4:1 for HBM4/HBM4E per relayed executive statement
numerical_basis.denominator: bit supply, not wafer starts; no die area, TSV yield or Nanya product mapping

primary_new_sources.counterevidence_or_limit: Secondary relay cites Investing.com transcript; no direct Micron filing/transcript in checked source. This is not evidence that Nanya has HBM production or a 3:1 company-level allocation.
